easy.def: Very, or to a great amount.
examples: I am so happy.
The soup is so hot.
She is so tall.

more.def: To a great degree, or very much.
examples: The night sky was so clear that we could see thousands of stars.
I was so tired after the hike that I fell asleep in the car.
Thank you so much for the lovely gift.

easy.def: A word that tells what happened because of something.
examples: It rained, so we stayed in.
I was hungry, so I ate.
He is sick, so he is home.

more.def: A word used to show that something happened as a result of what was just said.
examples: The bridge was closed, so we took a different road.
I forgot my lunch, so my friend shared hers with me.
The batteries were dead, so the toy stopped moving.

easy.def: A person in an army.
examples: The soldier wore a uniform.
Soldiers march.
He is a soldier.

more.def: A person who is a member of an army.
examples: The soldier stood guard at the gate.
Soldiers marched in the parade.
My grandpa was a soldier.

easy.def: A way to fix a problem.
examples: I found a solution. We can share the toy!
What is the solution to the math problem?
The solution was to ask for help.

more.def: The answer to a problem or the way to fix it.
examples: The solution to the puzzle was hidden in the last clue.
There is no easy solution to the traffic problem.
The class worked together to find a solution.

easy.def: An amount that is not all and not none.
examples: I want some milk.
Some kids are late.
She ate some of the cake.

more.def: An amount or number of something that is not stated exactly, or only part of a group.
examples: Some birds can fly very long distances without stopping.
I need some paper for my drawing.
We saw some deer near the river this morning.

easy.def: A person, but you do not say who.
examples: Somebody is at the door.
I need somebody to help.
Somebody ate my snack.

more.def: A person who is not named or is not known.
examples: Somebody left a pair of gloves on the bus.
I think somebody is knocking on the window.
We need somebody who can play the drums.

easy.def: A person, but you do not say who.
examples: Someone is at the door.
I need someone to help.
Someone took my pencil.

more.def: A person who is not named or is not known.
examples: Someone left a bag of apples on our porch.
I need someone to hold the other end of the rope.
Is there someone here who can read this sign?

easy.def: A thing that you do not know or name.
examples: I hear something.
She wants something to eat.
He found something shiny.

more.def: A thing that is not named or not known exactly.
examples: There is something under the bed, and I think it is the cat.
I would like to learn something new about space.
She whispered something to her friend.

easy.def: Not always, but now and then.
examples: Sometimes we eat dinner outside.
I sometimes ride my bike.
Sometimes it snows here.

more.def: At some times but not all of the time.
examples: Sometimes the bus is late when it rains.
My grandmother sometimes tells stories about when she was young.
Sea otters sometimes hold hands while they sleep.

easy.def: In a place you do not know.
examples: My shoes are somewhere here.
Let's go somewhere fun.
I left it somewhere.

more.def: In or to some place that is not named or known.
examples: I left my hat somewhere in the house.
Let's go somewhere warm for the holiday.
There must be a frog somewhere near the pond.

easy.def: A boy or man who is someone's child.
examples: He is their son.
The baker has a son.
Her son is five.

more.def: A boy or man in relation to his parents.
examples: The farmer and his son fed the cows together.
She is proud of her son, who won the spelling bee.
Their son plays the trumpet in the band.

easy.def: Words and music that people sing.
examples: We sing a song.
The bird's song is pretty.
My favorite song is on the radio.

more.def: A short piece of music with words that are sung.
examples: We learned a new song in music class.
The birds' morning song woke me.
She wrote a song about her dog.

easy.def: In a short time.
examples: Dinner is soon.
We will go soon.
She will be here soon.

more.def: In a short time from now, or not long after something.
examples: The bus will be here soon, so get your backpack.
Soon after the rain stopped, the sun came out.
I hope to see you again soon.

easy.def: Sad about something you did.
examples: I am sorry I was late.
She said sorry to me.
He felt sorry.

more.def: Feeling sad or ashamed about something you did, or sad for someone else.
examples: I am sorry that I broke your pencil.
We felt sorry for the lost puppy.
He said he was sorry for being rude.

easy.def: To put things into groups.
examples: Sort the socks by color.
We sorted the blocks.
I sort my cards.

more.def: To arrange things into groups or an order, by color, size or kind.
examples: We sorted the buttons by color and size.
The mail carrier sorts letters before delivering them.
Sort the words in alphabetical order.

easy.def: A kind or type.
examples: What sort of ice cream do you like?
This is a sort of bird.
Which sort of dog is that?

more.def: A kind or type of person or thing.
examples: What sort of music do you like to hear?
This sort of berry grows only in cold places.
He is the sort of friend who always shares.

easy.def: The deepest part of who a person is.
examples: Music touches my soul.
She has a kind soul.
A song can fill the soul.

more.def: The part of a person that some people believe is not the body, and holds feelings and thoughts.
examples: Many people believe the soul lives on after the body dies.
Music can touch the soul.
She has a kind and gentle soul.

easy.def: Something you hear.
examples: I hear a sound.
The sound was loud.
A bird makes a sound.

more.def: Something that you hear with your ears.
examples: The sound of rain on the roof put me to sleep.
A strange sound came from the attic.
Thunder is a loud sound that travels far.

easy.def: To seem a certain way when you hear it.
examples: That sounds fun.
It sounds loud.
She sounds happy.

more.def: To give a certain feeling when heard or told about.
examples: That plan sounds like a lot of fun.
Your voice sounds hoarse, so you should rest.
The idea sounded silly at first.

easy.def: The direction that is opposite of north.
examples: Geese fly south for winter.
We drove south to the beach.
The warm beaches are in the south.

more.def: The direction that is opposite to north, toward the bottom of most maps.
examples: Many birds fly south in the fall.
Florida is in the south of the United States.
At noon in the northern half of the world, the sun is in the south.
